rules.text: Stocks/use percentile is the same rank as the Fundamentals page: the share of every year on that sheet, including the current year, with stocks/use at or below this year. At or below the 33rd percentile is bullish. At or above the 67th is bearish. Otherwise neutral. World stocks/use is ending stocks divided by domestic use. A country uses ending stocks divided by domestic use plus exports. Canola uses the AAFC forecast stocks/use against the years on the Canada balance sheet, including the forecast year, or USDA Canada if that file is missing. If the latest ending-stocks revision moves the opposite way from the percentile, the cell becomes neutral.

Managed money net as a percent of open interest, ranked over the last 156 weeks. At or above the 85th percentile is extended long and reads bearish. At or below the 15th is extended short and reads bullish. Otherwise neutral. The cell shows the percent of open interest. Disaggregated managed money only. Leveraged Funds are not used.
Change in managed money net over one week and over four weeks. Both up is bullish. Both down is bearish. A mixed pair, or a zero change, is neutral.

Average of the Peak Trading Research weekly scores for the current week and the next four weeks. Scores run from −5 to +5. An average of 1 or higher is bullish. An average of -1 or lower is bearish. Otherwise neutral. The same scores are reused every year, keyed by calendar week, and a late-December window continues into January. They are typed on the Seasonals page, not fetched, and they do not expire. A market with no typed score is a dash. Peak Trading Research seasonal, last reviewed 2026-10-24.

Each signal cell is coloured on its own. Bullish is green and bearish is red. Neutral has no colour. The cell shows the figure only. A missing figure is a dash with no colour. There is no row total and no section score.

Export commitments versus a year ago, the same percent the Exports page uses. At least +5% is bullish. At least 5% below is bearish. Otherwise neutral. Canola uses CGC crop-year exports versus the same week a year ago, with the same band. Coffee and sugar have no series on the Exports page, so those cells are dashes.
CGC canola exports versus the same week a year ago. At least +5% is bullish and at least 5% below is bearish.
Stocks versus the 5-year average. At least +3% is bearish. At least 3% below is bullish. Natural gas uses the WNGSR published percent. Petroleum uses the percent computed from weekly levels.

This week's percent stock change minus the average percent change in the same week of the prior five years. At least +3 percentage points (a heavier build or a lighter draw) is bearish. At least 3 the other way is bullish.

Live cattle supply is Cattle on Feed on-feed head, percent of a year ago. Live cattle pipeline is Cattle on Feed marketings, percent of a year ago. Feeder supply is the Cattle report total of calves under 500 pounds and other steers and heifers outside feedlots, percent of a year ago. At or below 98 is bullish and at or above 102 is bearish. The percents are the ones the report prints. The semiannual figure stays current until 10 days after the next January 31 or July 31 release.
Feeder pipeline is Cattle on Feed placements, percent of a year ago, scored as demand for feeder cattle. At or above 102 is bullish and at or below 98 is bearish.

Choice boxed beef from the USDA AMS boxed-beef report is an official print, not a futures price. The file has a single print, so a four-week trend cannot be scored and the column is omitted. The figure stays in Key figures.
A cell whose as-of date is older than its cadence is a dash. Cadences, in days: wasde 45, aafc 45, cftc 14, exports 14, cgc 14, energy 14, weather 2, cattle 45.
